0.long_answer: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma (AITL) is known for its association with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV). Although EBV rarely infects the malignant T cells, it frequently infects the reactive B cells in the tumor microenvironment. This EBV infection of reactive B cells is thought to result from reduced T-cell immune surveillance and may contribute to further lymphoproliferative disorders in patients with AITL.

1.long_answer: The Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is most famously linked to infectious mononucleosis, commonly known as glandular fever. Although EBV has been associated with several types of lymphoproliferative disorders, such as certain T-cell and B-cell lymphomas (for example, angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma), the disease it most commonly causes is infectious mononucleosis. This condition typically presents with symptoms like fever, sore throat, swollen lymph glands, and fatigue, especially affecting adolescents and young adults.
